topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the practical tie-ins, historical context, and learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Tumor Viruses and Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: They trace how the historical study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for measuring cell transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, Tumor Suppressors, and Cell Cycle Regulation
topics.groupedBecause: They define the functional and genetic characteristics of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes and illustrate their effects on cell cycle checkpoints.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Sequence and Chromosomal Instability
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the distinct forms of genetic instability in cancer and the specific defects in DNA repair, replication, and chromosome segregation that generate them.

topics.label: Multi-Step Tumor Progression and Hereditary Predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the multi-step model of tumor development and how inherited cancer predispositions and ongoing mutations shape tumor progression and evolution.

topics.label: Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session by reviewing learning outcomes, offering reading recommendations, and previewing the next lecture.
